title: Floor Zones A–F
before:
1. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Inbound Operators work in Zone A to unload, count and inspect deliveries before booking. Vehicles assigned to Zone A use docks 1-4 only. No outbound staging takes place in Zone A.

2. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Put-away from Zone A moves directly to Zone B rack locations. Stock in Zone B supplies replenishment to Zone C. Access in Zone B follows rack aisle controls.

3. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Pickers operate in Zone C against scanner tasks to fulfil customer orders. Replenishment keeps Zone C pick faces filled from Zone B. Packing preparation also starts from picks completed in Zone C.

4. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Outbound loads are staged, wrapped and released in Zone D. Dispatchers assign docks 5-8 for loading in Zone D. Carriers collect only from Zone D doors.

5. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Product requiring temperature control is stored only in Zone E. Doors to Zone E remain closed except for put-away and picking moves. Monitoring keeps Zone E within its +2 to +8 °C range.

6. Zone F holds the value-added services area. The quarantine area is in Zone F for holds pending release. Returns are inspected in Zone F before any disposition. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F for segregated storage. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

Circulation between zones uses the marked aisle network.

7. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. These aisles link Zone A through Zone B and Zone C to Zone D, with branches to Zone E and Zone F. Counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks use main transport aisles for longer moves. Keep main transport aisles clear of staging at all times.

8. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are located inside Zone B between high-bay runs. Only materials handling equipment and authorised persons enter rack storage aisles when handling pallets.

9. Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide. Walkways provide protected routes through and around Zone A, Zone B, Zone C, Zone D, Zone E and Zone F. Do not block segregated pedestrian walkways with pallets, cages or waste. Cross only at marked crossing points.

title: System Booking and Release to Put-Away
before:
1. Apply PR-01 Inbound receiving to close the receiving task in Zone A and apply PR-02 Put-away to storage to release pallets to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. No pallet leaves Zone A for put-away until both procedures are satisfied in order.

2. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Complete the count and inspection fully and resolve discrepancies on the inbound paperwork before creating any system booking. Do not book damaged, short or unidentified stock as available.

3. Observe the booking sequence:
   a. Inspection, then system booking. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01.
   b. System booking, then put-away. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage under PR-02.
   Follow this order for every pallet without exception.

4. Book receipts on the WMS using the handheld scanners. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; return the device to its charge bay after booking and report any scanning failure to the shift supervisor immediately. Enter the exact quantity verified at inspection, the pallet ID, and the storage requirement indicated on the purchase order or product master.

5. Assign the put-away destination at booking:
   a. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Use for general ambient pallets.
   b. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Use only for temperature-controlled product and confirm the cold-chain status is intact.
   c. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Use for labelling, kitting or other value-added work instructed on the receipt.
   Direct the forklift operator to the assigned zone on the WMS put-away task. Do not stage pallets for Zone B, Zone E or Zone F outside their designated lanes.

6. Route exceptions to quarantine or hazmat holding:
   a. Move any pallet failing inspection, requiring quality review, or awaiting approval to the quarantine area in Zone F. Hold it on system status quarantine.
   b. Move packaged hazardous material requiring segregation to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. Hold it on system status hazmat hold.
   Do not book quarantine or hazmat pallets as available for sale and do not put them away to Zone B or Zone E.

7. Release the put-away task only when the WMS shows status booked and the destination zone is confirmed. Attach the signed inbound receipt to the booking record in PR-01, then generate the PR-02 put-away task. Hand over the pallets with scanner confirmation at the Zone A boundary.

title: Cold Zone E
before:
1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Hold only chilled product in Zone E and keep doors closed except for put-away and picking moves.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check the automated monitoring display on entry and do not store product if the reading is below the minimum.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat any reading above the maximum as an incident under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and notify the shift supervisor immediately.

4. Manually verify cold-zone temperature each shift. Record the manual reading, time and initials on the Zone E temperature log and countersign any corrective action.

5. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A. Keep chilled goods staged in Zone A only for the time needed to complete inspection.

6. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every chilled inbound. Prioritise chilled pallets for inspection and move them to Zone E without delay after release.

7. Complete system booking before put-away to storage. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for the booking sequence: goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage.

8. Do not put away unbooked pallets to Zone E. Confirm the storage location in the WMS, then transport the pallet directly to the assigned cold location.

9. Observe the pallet limit for all Zone E put-away. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg; reject or split any pallet exceeding this weight before put-away.

10. Store pallets to preserve airflow and temperature stability. Keep pallets off door thresholds, maintain circulation gaps and return monitoring probes to position after each move.

11. Report any temperature alarm, door fault or product exposure to the shift supervisor for review under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Quarantine affected stock and do not pick or dispatch until cleared.

title: Cycle Counting
before:
1. Execute PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts for cycle counting on every working day. Follow the rotating zone schedule without omission.

2. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments. Apply that duty throughout PR-08.

3. Count daily across all storage areas:
   a. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
   b. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
   c. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
   d. Zone F holds the value-added services area.

4. Plan the rotating zone schedule so each zone is counted in rotation. Issue count tasks in the WMS at shift start and assign a stock controller as count owner.

5. Perform counts with handheld WMS scanners. Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners; coordinate scanner allocation with the shift supervisor to maintain coverage of PR-08 counts alongside receiving and picking.

6. Scan each location and product systematically. Do not post any adjustment from the first count alone.

7. Investigate every variance immediately:
   a. Check adjacent locations, overstock, and recent put-away or replenishment moves.
   b. Verify against inbound receipts, pick tasks and dispatch staging.
   c. For Zone E, verify the location while maintaining the +2 to +8 °C condition and report any temperature excursion separately.

8. Execute the recount rule: a second count happens BEFORE any stock adjustment is posted (PR-08). Assign the recount to a second checker where possible and record both results in the WMS.

9. Hold adjustments until verified. After the recount, present unresolved variances to the warehouse manager for review. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results and authorise the posting of adjustments.

10. Post approved adjustments in the WMS with reason code, location, product, quantity, counter names and approval reference. Retain scanner logs and recount sheets with the PR-08 record.

11. Close the daily cycle count in the WMS, update the rotating zone schedule, and handover outstanding variances to the next shift stock controller.

title: Cold-Chain and Hazmat Response
before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every activity in Zone E. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.

2. Maintain the cold zone within its limits at all times. Keep the temperature at or above +2 °C. Keep the temperature at or below +8 °C.

3. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift. Record the reading, the time and the verifier on the shift log. Do not rely on automated monitoring alone.

4. Respond immediately to any temperature alarm or out-of-range reading under PR-12 Cold-chain handling:
   a) Recheck the reading at the calibrated display inside Zone E.
   b) Keep doors closed and restrict entry while the check is repeated.
   c) Notify the shift supervisor without delay. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
   d) Hold affected stock inside Zone E and tag it pending decision.
   e) Do not move chilled goods to another zone until the shift supervisor authorises release.

5. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response to all hazmat receipts, storage and movements. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F. The hazmat cage inside Zone F covers 60 m2.

6. Observe storage limits for the hazmat cage. Store no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time. Calculate capacity on full-weight pallets: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg, so the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.

7. Stage hazmat only inside the cage. Do not exceed the floor limit. Keep incompatible classes segregated in accordance with PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response safety data sheets.

8. Execute spill response under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response as follows:
   a) Stop work and alert nearby personnel.
   b) Notify the shift supervisor immediately for incident response.
   c) Ventilate the area and isolate the spill. Do not wash spills into drains.
   d) Don appropriate PPE and deploy the spill kit for the material class.
   e) Contain, absorb and collect the material for safe disposal. Log the incident, quantity and corrective action.

9. Record every PR-12 Cold-chain handling verification and every PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response event in the WMS. Report any limit breach, equipment fault or stock at risk to the shift supervisor for follow-up.

title: 3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)
before:
3.1 Cold Zone Work (Zone E)

1. Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. This segregated chilled area operates inside the warehouse floor covering 6,000 m2 and is reserved solely for goods requiring continuous chilled storage. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every entry, movement and storage activity affecting Zone E.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times. Check that doors close fully after each transit and never wedge or prop them open. Report any ice build-up, seal damage or prolonged door opening that could drive temperature below the lower limit.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times. Treat any reading above this upper limit as a cold-chain deviation. Initiate the response required under PR-12 Cold-chain handling immediately and prevent further warm air ingress until the area has stabilised.

4. Verify temperature manually each shift. Observe the calibrated display inside Zone E, record the reading with time and initials in the shift log, and compare it against the +2 to +8 °C range. Escalate out-of-range results without delay and retain the record for traceability.

5. Minimise exposure and keep the chamber closed. Plan picks and put-away to reduce entries, enter only when the task is ready, and exit promptly after completion. Allow doors to self-close and confirm engagement before leaving the area.

6. Wear mandatory personal protection on every warehouse floor task, including all Zone E work. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and must be fully fastened and visible before entry.

7. Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor, including inside the cold zone. Inspect footwear for secure fastening and intact soles, and move carefully where condensation or moisture may make surfaces slippery.

8. Limit Zone E access to personnel trained in PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Inform the supervisor before entering for extended tasks and maintain visual or radio contact so assistance can be summoned. Do not use the cold zone for breaks, storage of ambient goods or non-chilled equipment.

9. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Direct every temperature alarm, failed verification, access problem or incident inside Zone E to the shift supervisor for immediate review and coordinated response.

10. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Refer repeated deviations, equipment faults, unresolved alarms and any cold-chain risk affecting product integrity to the warehouse manager for decision and sign-off.

11. Contain suspected breaches inside Zone E. Hold affected stock in place, tag it clearly as pending cold-chain decision, and prevent movement to other zones until authorised release is given under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

title: 1.2 Shift Supervisor - Shift Leadership and Incident Ownership
before:
1. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2. Shift coverage is 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 1 and 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday for Shift 2; the supervisor on duty is accountable for all floor activity during those hours.
3. Duties of the role:
  1) Direct forklift operators, pickers, inbound operators and other floor staff across all operating areas: Zone A the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, Zone B the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, Zone C the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks, Zone D the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8, Zone E the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.
  2) Maintain discipline on PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse, PR-14 Emergency evacuation and PR-15 End-of-shift handover, and ensure briefings are completed at every handover.
  3) Enforce site PPE and MHE rules: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, and forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
  4) Verify operational checks on shift: cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift; confirm readings are logged and escalate deviations immediately.
4. Incident and emergency ownership:
  1) Review every incident report without exception and close actions with documented follow-up.
  2) Lead evacuations under PR-14 Emergency evacuation, account for staff at the assembly point and apply the sequence that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
  3) Ensure an evacuation drill runs every quarter and attendance and learnings are recorded.
5. Quality and compliance decisions:
  1) Approve the final disposition of inspected returns; returns are inspected in Zone F and the supervisor determines restock, rework or scrap.
  2) Hold all goods awaiting disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling in the quarantine area in Zone F.
  3) Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR; damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.
6. Site integrity:
  1) Ensure racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and defects are quarantined and reported.
  2) Coordinate with the dispatcher and warehouse manager to keep receiving, storage, picking and dispatch flows aligned across Zone A, Zone B, Zone C and Zone D.

title: 2.2 Inbound Operator - Receiving, Inspection and Put-Away
before:
1. Purpose of the role: unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-02 Put-away to storage, and transfer accepted stock to the correct storage zone without breach of weight, temperature or hazmat limits.

2. Work location and scope: operate solely in Zone A, the receiving zone covering inbound docks 1-4 for unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving; do not receive inbound goods at any other door. Hand over released pallets only to the designated storage zones: Zone B for bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F which holds the value-added services area.

Reject damaged, leaking or suspected non-conforming stock from booking and segregate it for quarantine instruction. Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system under PR-01. Do not pre-book unchecked pallets.

8. Perform PR-02 Put-away to storage only after system booking. Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Print and apply system-directed labels, confirm location tasks on the scanner, and move pallets to the WMS-directed bay in Zone B or other assigned zone. Do not stage inbound stock in aisles or dispatch areas as put-away.

9. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for chilled inbound. Transfer accepted chilled goods immediately to Zone E, the cold zone held at +2 to +8 °C. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C. Keep cold-chain pallets closed, minimise door openings, and record handover to Zone E so temperature control is maintained.

10. Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for hazmat receipts. Route directed hazmat to the hazmat cage inside Zone F. The hazmat cage covers 60 m2 inside Zone F and no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage stock on the WMS before put-away and do not exceed the limit. If leaking, odorous or damaged hazmat is found, stop work, contain the area and alert the shift supervisor; do not inspect or open damaged hazmat on the general bench.

11. Maintain inbound discipline: keep Zone A clear for inspection and unloading, return equipment and scanners to charge, and ensure all inspected goods are either booked and tasked for put-away or formally segregated before leaving the zone at shift end.

title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

title: 3.3 Temperature-Controlled Storage SLA
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd commits to provide chilled storage in Zone E as the designated cold zone. Zone E is the cold zone for chilled storage and is held at +2 to +8 °C.

2. We guarantee that the cold zone will be maintained within the contracted temperature range at all times while goods are in storage. The cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +8 °C, in accordance with product requirements for chilled goods held in Zone E.

3. Temperature control is provided continuously during all operating hours. Chilled goods are stored only in Zone E and are not co-mingled with ambient storage, and all handling into and out of Zone E is performed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

4. Manual verification of cold-zone temperature is performed each shift as a contracted service level. A trained operative records the calibrated reading for Zone E on the temperature log at least once per shift, and any out-of-range reading is escalated immediately under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

5. Verification coverage aligns with the warehouse operating pattern. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, providing two manual verifications per working day. No shift will close without its cold-zone verification entry.

6. PR-12 Cold-chain handling defines the full handling rules for Zone E, including temperature monitoring, door discipline, alarm response and hold-and-release of affected stock. All client goods stored in Zone E are handled solely under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and no deviation is permitted without written client approval.

7. Equipment reliability for the cold zone is supported by scheduled maintenance. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs, including refrigeration plant, doors, seals and monitoring devices serving Zone E. All faults affecting Zone E are logged and prioritised to protect the +2 to +8 °C range.

8. Overall accountability for cold-chain performance rests with site leadership. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, and retains final sign-off for cold-chain compliance, temperature records and any service credits arising from temperature excursions in Zone E.

9. Records of temperature verification for Zone E are retained and made available to the client on request. Each record shows date, shift, time, reading and operative, and is traceable to PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
